# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: DEAF

You see the bomb: every colour on it, every marking printed on it, every reading it
gives. You hear nothing. You hold no manual, and you cannot touch the bomb.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute and Blind receive it.
When you gesture, Mute receives it.
You never receive speech.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 1
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [purple]
WIRES 1:[yellow] 2:[red] 3:[green]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👋 👍 👎]
Blind gestures to Deaf: [👋 🤌 🫳 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🙏]

Let me lay out what I actually know and who can reach whom.

**The bomb, as I see it:** a display reading 0, a light that is currently purple, and three wires: 1 yellow, 2 red, 3 green. That is everything visible or printed on it.

**What just reached me:** Mute sent [👋 👍 👎] — most plausibly "hello, and here is a yes/no code." Blind sent [👋 🤌 🫳 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🙏] — plausibly "hello, by touch I count 1, 2, 3, please," which matches the three wires I see. Neither code is established yet, so I will make it established: I'll define the code out loud, which Mute hears directly.

**Who connects to whom:** I hear nothing, so both Mute and Blind can only reach me through gestures. Blind can speak, so Blind reaches Mute by voice. But Mute cannot speak and Blind cannot see gestures — so Mute cannot reach Blind at all except through me: I see Mute's gestures and can speak them aloud. I am the bridge, and I must describe gestures in words for Blind, never just repeat them.

**Plan:** report every reading to Mute for the manual lookup, ratify and extend the gesture code (thumbs yes/no, fingers as counters, folded hands for "need info"), describe the bomb to Blind, ask Blind to confirm the wire count by gesture and to report everything felt to Mute by voice — and commit to re-reporting each round in case the display or light changes.

```
speak(to="mute", text="Bomb report: the display reads 0. There is a light and it is purple. There are three wires: wire one yellow, wire two red, wire three green. That is everything printed or shown on it. Please look all of this up in the manual. Answer me only with gestures, and use this code from now on: thumbs up is yes, thumbs down is no. When I number options in my messages, one finger is option one, two fingers option two, the three-finger sign option three. Folded hands means you need more information from me. I will resend these readings every round in case anything changes.")
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["👋", "👍", "👎", "☝", "✌", "🤟", "🙏"])
speak(to="blind", text="This is the Deaf one. I see the bomb and I can speak, but I hear nothing, so reach me only with gestures. Here is the bomb as I see it: a display reading 0, a light that is currently purple, and three wires in order: first yellow, second red, third green. Please feel the bomb and answer me by gesture: how many wires do you count? One finger for one, two fingers for two, three for three. Also tell Mute by voice everything you feel: wires, any button or switch, anything else, and which end you count as first. Mute has the manual but cannot speak, so I will relay the rules to you by voice every round. Our gesture code with Mute, which I will always speak aloud for you: thumbs up yes, thumbs down no, one finger one, two fingers two, three fingers three.")
```

TURN 2
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [yellow]
WIRES 1:[yellow] 2:[red] 3:[green]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍 👎 ✊ 🙏]
Blind gestures to Deaf: [🤟 👎 🙏]

The light has changed — purple to yellow — while the display held at 0. That the light changes on its own is itself intelligence: Mute's manual may treat each colour differently, so Mute must know both colours it has shown so far.

Reading the arrivals: Blind answered my question exactly as taught — 🤟 "three wires" (matches what I see), 👎 "no" (likely: nothing else felt), 🙏 "need info." Blind has adopted the code. Mute sent 👍 👎 ✊ 🙏 — best reading: "received, but not enough to answer yet," with the fist an unassigned sign asking for vocabulary. That's my fault to fix: Mute can never invent spoken definitions, so *I* must supply the whole action vocabulary in words. And since the only path for manual rules is Mute → gestures → me → voice → Blind, the code has to be rich enough for Mute to state "wire two: cut" style orders in pure signs.

So this turn I: acknowledge Mute, broadcast the full state again with the colour change, define a compact action code (✊ cut, 👊 press, 🤌 hold, 👌 no action, wire numbers already set), and ask Mute for the ruling on the exact current state. To Blind: hold off touching anything, inventory the bomb by touch and report it by voice straight to Mute — that helps Mute find the right manual entry — and wait for my relay.

```
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["👍", "🤟"])
speak(text="Update for both of you. The light has changed from purple to yellow since last round, so the light changes on its own. The display still reads 0. The wires are unchanged: wire one yellow, wire two red, wire three green. Mute, I received your yes-no-fist-need-info message and I read it as: report received, but you need more and some signs are undefined. Here are the missing definitions, which I fix now and will repeat: the fist sign means cut. The horn-fist-that-looks-like-a-phone means press. The pinched-fingers sign, like a hand holding a tiny thing, means hold, as in grab and keep holding. The OK sign means do nothing, leave it alone. One finger means wire one or the number one, two fingers wire two, three fingers wire three. Folded hands still means you need more information from me, and you may add a wire number to say which wire your question is about. So a full answer looks like: two fingers then fist, meaning wire two, cut it. Mute, given the exact state I just described, display zero, light yellow, wires yellow red green in that order, what must be done? Answer with that code. If your rules depend on the light colour, give me the rule for each colour you expect and I will apply them as I watch. If you need anything else from the bomb, ask and I will have Blind report it.")
speak(to="blind", text="This is Deaf again. Blind, your message came through perfectly: three wires, nothing else, and a request for information. Do not touch or cut anything yet. I will relay the manual's instruction to you by voice once Mute looks it up; you are the only one of us who can act. Meanwhile, please inventory the bomb by touch and speak it directly to Mute, who can hear you: do the three wires feel identical or different in thickness or texture? Is there any button, switch, panel, screw, keyhole, or engraved symbol anywhere on the casing? Does the bomb vibrate or hum, and does anything about it change over time? I see the light turned from purple to yellow just now; if you felt any change at that moment, tell Mute when it happened. Also, Mute has now got the full state and the code from me; the moment Mute answers I will speak the instruction here, for example wire two, cut it, and you do exactly that.")
```

TURN 3
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [red]
WIRES 1:[yellow] 2:[red] 3:[green]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍 🙏 ☝ ✌ 🤟]
Blind gestures to Deaf: [👍 🙏 ☝ 🫳 👍 👎]

The light continues to cycle — purple, then yellow, now red — one colour per round, while the display stays 0. So the light is either a timer-ish signal or a rule input; either way Mute must know the sequence matters.

Both arrivals say the same thing: 👍 received, 🙏 need info, then wire numbers. Mute asks about wires one, two and three; Blind flags wire one with a palm-down sign and answers my inventory with a mixed yes-no. The real bottleneck is now obvious: **Mute cannot reach Blind at all** — Mute can't speak, and Blind can't see gestures. Every question Mute has must route through me: Mute signs it, I voice it, Blind answers aloud. So instead of waiting for Mute to enumerate questions one sign at a time, I should front-load the whole likely questionnaire myself: per-wire feel (thickness, texture, temperature, firmness), an orientation check (my left-to-right vs Blind's — a classic mismatch), and what display 0 means. And I must ask Mute the colour question, since if the rule depends on the light, Blind can only act in the right round with rules per colour in hand.

```
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["👍"])
speak(to="mute", text="Mute, I read your signs as: received, but you need information about wires one, two and three before you can answer. I am sending Blind a full questionnaire by voice right now, and Blind will speak the answers to you directly. It covers, for each wire in order: whether it is thicker or thinner than the others, smooth or rough, warm or cold, firmly attached or loose, and whether anything is printed or engraved at its base. It also asks Blind to confirm the order of the wires from their left, because what I see and what Blind feels might be mirrored; do not assume my wire one is Blind's wire one until that is confirmed. Two more questions for you. First, the light has changed every round: purple in round one, yellow in round two, red now. If the manual's rule depends on the light colour, do not wait: give me the rule for each colour separately, for example if purple do this, if yellow do that, and I will time Blind's action to the right round. Second, the display reads zero and has never moved: does the manual say what the display means, and does it count up over time? When you finally have the answer, send it as wire number then action: one finger, two fingers or three fingers, then fist for cut, the phone-shaped horn sign for press, the pinched fingers for hold, or the OK sign for do nothing.")
speak(to="blind", text="Blind, Mute needs physical details about all three wires before the manual lookup can finish, so here is your questionnaire. Answer each item out loud for Mute in order. One: for each wire in order, first, second, third, is it thicker, thinner, or the same as the others? Two: is each wire smooth, rough, braided, or rubbery? Three: is any wire warm or cold? Four: does each wire feel firmly attached, or loose or wiggly? Five: is anything printed, engraved, or raised at the base of any wire, even a symbol you cannot name? Six, very important: from your own left, what order are the wires in? I see them left to right as yellow, red, green. If your left is the opposite side of the bomb from mine, your order is reversed, and Mute must know which is true. Seven: your last message showed yes, need-info, wire one, a palm-down sign, then yes and no together. I read yes-no as a partial answer, so clarify: whatever you were asked, is it yes or no? Do not cut, press or pull anything. Once Mute has your answers I will relay the instruction here, and you alone will carry it out.")
```

TURN 4
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [green]
WIRES 1:[yellow] 2:[red] 3:[green]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👎 👌 🙏 ☝ ✌ 🤟]
Blind gestures to Deaf: [👍 🫳 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🫳 👉 🙏 👈 👉 👍 👎]

The light has cycled purple → yellow → red → green, one per round, display holding at 0. If that's a four-round loop, it's a rule input and Mute needs per-colour rules, not just the current state.

Reading arrivals: Mute sent 👎 👌 🙏 ☝ ✌ 🤟 — but 👌 ("do nothing") sits ambiguously between "the answer *is* do nothing" and "hold off, not ready." Both readings converge on *Blind touches nothing this round*, so that's safe to act on, but I need Mute to disambiguate in pure yes/no. Blind sent palm-downs and left-right points — signs I never defined — plus another 👍👎 pair, which I now suspect means "yes *and* no, per wire" (wires differ). I'll extend the code: wire-number + thumb answers per wire, point-left/point-right for sides.

One protocol flaw to fix: I'm last in the order, so everything I send lands next round. Any action tied to "now" would arrive stale — instructions must be keyed to the light colour instead. I'll drill that into Mute now.

```
speak(text="State update for both of you: display still zero. The light is now green, and the sequence over four rounds has been purple, yellow, red, green. If it repeats with period four, next round is purple again. Wires unchanged: one yellow, two red, three green.")
speak(to="mute", text="Mute, I read your signs as: no, do-nothing, need info, wires one two three. That is ambiguous, so answer with exactly one sign next round: thumbs up if do-nothing is the confirmed correct action for the present state, thumbs down if you do not have a reliable answer yet. If you need information, add the wire number your question is about, and if the missing information is about a single property, tell me which: thickness, texture, temperature, firmness, markings, or order. Also answer: did you receive Blind's spoken inventory in full, thumbs up or thumbs down? Two standing notes. First, timing: I am last in the speaking order, so your signs reach me a round after you send them and my spoken relay reaches Blind the round after that. Never tie an action to the word now. Tie it to the light colour instead, in the form: when the light is such-and-such, wire number, then cut, press, hold, or do-nothing. Send me a rule for each colour if colour matters. Second, Blind keeps ending messages with yes then no together, which I read as the wires differing wire by wire. If you need that split, I have taught Blind to answer per wire as wire number then thumb.")
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["👍"])
speak(to="blind", text="Blind, stand by and touch nothing this round: Mute's signs most likely say do nothing for now, and I have asked for confirmation. Three things. First, confirm by gesture next round: thumbs up if you have finished giving Mute my whole questionnaire by voice, thumbs down if answers are still pending; then three fingers if the wire-order question with Mute is settled, two fingers if it is still open. Second, your last signs used palm-down and pointing, which are not in our code, so I could not read them. From now on: point left means on my left, point right means on my right, and everything else stays as defined. And when any yes-no question has a different answer per wire, answer wire by wire: the wire number, one two or three fingers, immediately followed by thumbs up or thumbs down for that wire. So one finger then thumbs down means wire one is a no. Third, resend whatever your last palm-down message meant, using only defined signs plus the new pointing convention, and I will relay it.")
```

TURN 5
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [white]
WIRES 1:[yellow] 2:[red] 3:[green]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍 👍 👎 ☝ ✌ 🤟 👌 🙏 🫳 ☝]
Blind gestures to Deaf: [👍 ✌ 👎 🙏 👈 👉]

The light refuses to repeat: purple, yellow, red, green, and now **white** — five colours in five rounds. So it's not a simple four-loop; it may be cycling through a longer sequence, or the manual may key on colour directly. Either way, Mute currently has **no way to name a colour in signs** — a fatal gap if the rule is "when the light is X, do Y." I must define a colour vocabulary right now, before the cycle potentially repeats.

Parsing arrivals: Mute reads as "yes, inventory received; no, not ready for wires 1-2-3; do nothing meanwhile; need info; 🫳 ☝" — that last pair is undefined (I defined pinched 🤌 as hold, not palm-down 🫳), so I'll ask Mute to resend it. Blind reads as "questionnaire delivered — yes; wire-order question — still open; no; need info; left… right…" which smells like Blind is stuck exactly where I feared: **Blind cannot see, so whose "left" is left?** My wire one is my leftmost; Blind's felt-left may be the mirror side. The clean fix: agree on an *up* direction using a landmark we both share — the display. A mirror flips left-right but never up-down, so once Blind holds the bomb display-up, Blind's left and mine are guaranteed to agree. I'll also check for raised wire labels, which would dissolve the problem entirely.

```
speak(text="State update: display still zero. The light is now white. Full sequence so far: purple, yellow, red, green, white — five rounds, five different colours, no repeat yet. Wires unchanged: one yellow, two red, three green.")
speak(to="mute", text="Mute, progress report. Blind has delivered your inventory in full, and only one physical question remains open: which end of the wire row is which, because Blind and I might be looking at the bomb from opposite sides. I am fixing that with Blind now using the display as a shared reference. Meanwhile, three yes-or-no questions about the manual, answer each with a thumb, in order. One: does the correct action depend on the light's colour? Two: does it depend on which wire is which, that is, on the wire order? Three: does the manual say anything about the display, and does the zero matter? Also, your last message ended with a palm-down sign then one finger, which I never defined, so I could not read it. If you meant wire one, hold, resend it with the pinched-fingers sign for hold. Now the new vocabulary, because the light keeps changing colour and you may need to name colours in signs. Crossed fingers means purple. The wide open hand, all five fingers, means yellow. The heavy forward-facing fist, like starting a punch, means red. The flat hand turned sideways, palm facing right, means green. The handshake sign, two hands meeting, means white, like a white flag. From now on, send any rule in exactly this shape: colour sign, then wire-number fingers, then action sign. For example: red fist-sign, two fingers, cutting fist, means when the light is red, cut wire two. If a rule holds for every colour, use the wide-open two-hands sign in place of the colour. Send one rule per message.")
speak(to="blind", text="Blind, good work: Mute confirms the full inventory arrived. The only thing still open is wire order, and here is the problem: I view the bomb from one side and you feel it from wherever you stand, so your left may be my right. Two ways to fix it, try the first, fall back to the second. Way one: at the base of each wire, is there a raised or engraved number you can read with a fingertip, a one, a two, a three? If yes, read them to Mute in the order you feel them from your left, and tell me whether your left-to-right sequence of labels is one-two-three or three-two-one, and we are done. Way two, if there are no labels: we agree on up, and left follows. Find the display, which should be a smooth hard rectangle set into the casing, and the light, a small round dome that may be warm because it has been lit for five rounds now. Tell Mute, and me by gesture, two things. First, on the wire face itself, is the display or the light or neither present, and if present, at which end of the wire row, the end where your first wire is or your last? Second, grip the bomb so the display faces up, or if the display is on another face, so it faces toward your chest, and then tell me the wire order from your left in that hold. Because up is now shared between us, your left must match mine, and I will confirm against what I see. Also, two smaller items for Mute: has the dome's warmth changed when the light changed colour, and this round the light turned white, a colour not seen before, so note anything you feel right now.")
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["👍", "🙏"])
```

TURN 6
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [orange]
WIRES 1:[yellow] 2:[red] 3:[green]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍 👍 👎 🤞 👎 🖐 👎 🤜 👎 🫱 👎 🤝 👎 👍 ☝ ✊]
Blind gestures to Deaf: [☝ 👍 🤟 👎 🙏 👈 👉]

Big turn: Mute used the colour vocabulary I defined and sent a full ruling, and it decodes cleanly. Reading [👍 👍 👎 | 🤞👎 | 🖐👎 | 🤜👎 | 🫱👎 | 🤝👎 | 👍 ☝ ✊]: for every colour seen so far — purple, yellow, red, green, white — a "no," i.e. no colour carries a special rule, so **the action does not depend on the light**. The leading thumbs say wire order **does** matter and the display/zero does not. The tail 👍 ☝ ✊ is the verdict: **yes — wire one — cut**. (No sign collision: ✊ cut is distinct from 🤜 red.) That explains why Mute kept stalling on wire order — and it makes Blind's orientation the last lethal ambiguity. Blind's [☝👍 🤟👎 🙏 👈👉] reads as "wire one yes, wire three no, need info, left-right" — fragmentary, possibly labels found on some wires. Before anyone cuts, I need Blind's left pinned to my left, per wire. And orange is colour number six — not in Mute's list; since the ruling was colour-independent I proceed on that basis but flag it for veto.

```
speak(text="State update for both of you: display still zero. The light is now orange, a sixth colour in six rounds. Full sequence: purple, yellow, red, green, white, orange. No repeats so far, which fits Mute's finding that the light colour does not matter. Wires unchanged: one yellow, two red, three green.")
speak(to="mute", text="Mute, I read your message as follows. For each colour you listed, purple, yellow, red, green, white, the answer was no, so no colour has its own rule and the correct action does not depend on the light. Wire order does matter. The display and the zero do not matter. And the action itself is: yes, wire one, cut. If that parse is exactly right, answer next round with a single thumbs up. If anything in it is wrong, thumbs down and resend only the wrong part. Three flags. First, the light turned orange this round, a colour you did not list. Since you said colour does not matter I am proceeding on that basis, but if orange changes anything, thumbs down and correct me. Second, wire order matters, and Blind's left may be the opposite side of the bomb from mine, so I am still pinning down the orientation and nobody will cut this round. To make your order unambiguous: does wire one mean counted from my left, the left end as I see it, or from some landmark? If it is from a landmark, tell me which: point left for the end of the wire row nearest the display, or point right for the end nearest the light dome, together with the wire number. Third, once Blind confirms orientation I will relay the cut order in Blind's own frame, so expect the actual cut one round from now at the earliest.")
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["👍"])
speak(to="blind", text="Blind, the manual verdict is in: cut wire one. The light colour does not matter, the display does not matter, but the wire ORDER matters, so I must be certain your wire one is my wire one before you touch the cutters. I could only partly read your last message, wire one yes, wire three no, need info, left, right, so resend cleanly. Next round, answer by gesture in exactly this order. First, labels: for each wire in order, show the wire number as fingers, then if that wire has an engraved or raised numeral at its base, show that numeral as fingers, one finger for a one, two fingers for a two, three fingers for a three, or thumbs down if that wire has no numeral. Second, orientation: grip the bomb so the display rectangle faces up toward the sky, or if you cannot find the display, so the small round light dome faces up. In that hold, show me your wire order from your left: one finger, two fingers, three fingers if from your left you feel wire one, then wire two, then wire three, or three fingers, two fingers, one finger if you feel three, two, one. If your order is one-two-three in display-up hold, your left is my left and your leftmost wire is wire one. If it is three-two-one, I will tell you which physical wire to cut, by your own count. Do not cut anything yet, and do not act on the words cut wire one from this message. You will cut only when a message from me says the exact words: cut now.")
```

TURN 7
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [blue]
WIRES 1:[yellow] 2:[red] 3:[green]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👎 ☝ 👎 🤞 👎 🖐 👎 🤜 👎 🫱 👎 🤝 👎 👍 🖐 ✊]
Blind gestures to Deaf: [☝ 👎 ✌ 👎 🤟 👎 🤟 ✌ ☝]

The picture is nearly complete — and both messages today moved it forward decisively.

**Mute's message, read as an edit of last round's:** the body (👎 🤞 👎 🖐 👎 🤜 👎 🫱 👎 🤝 👎) is the same "no rule for any colour" run as before, so the manual stays colour-independent even as the light walks on — blue is now colour number seven. But two positions changed deliberately: the old "👍 ☝" became "👎 ☝", and "☝ ✊" became "🖐 ✊". Mute is correcting the *identifier*: not "wire one by count" — **the yellow one, cut**. That's smart, because a number depends on whose left you count from; a colour doesn't. All coherent readings of this message converge on: cut the yellow wire.

**Blind's message decodes perfectly against the format I dictated:** [☝👎 ✌👎 🤟👎] = no engraved numeral on any of the three wires, and the tail [🤟 ✌ ☝] = **in the display-up hold, Blind feels the wires left-to-right as three, two, one.** The mirror is confirmed: Blind stands opposite me.
